confirmations.listener: fairly clear, can hear the amplification
same as before, very clear, amplification works - a big step forward

what_changed_relative_to_everything_befo: the stale 57-frame-mismatched coefficients were removed, so the loop is a plain feedback loop instead of a badly predistorted one
digital gain -8 dB instead of -14 dB (6 dB louder than the point that was always inaudible)
talker moved to about 5 cm from the microphone
remaining_limitation_reported_by_the_lis: near the speaker the amplified sound is still not louder than the source, because -8 dB digital gain means the output is 8 dB BELOW the microphone signal; positive net gain is needed for the speaker to dominate
why_more_gain_is_hard: the loop rings around 250-470 Hz. Raising the talker level raises the output AND the feedback by the same amount, so close-talk does not improve the ratio; at 5 cm the mode share rose from 0.12 (15 cm) to 0.36-0.42, i.e. closer to regeneration
the_only_structural_lever_left: suppress the 250-470 Hz band inside the loop (high-pass or low-shelf cut). That buys gain headroom without touching speech band gain
ownership: a filter in the loop is a coefficient/algorithm change -> B designs it; A loads and runs the board comparison; C owns the measurement protocol
not_claimed: no claim that the current point is the optimum
no claim about listener intelligibility beyond the two confirmations above
